thread.title: Attorney General Bird leads coalition urging credit card companies to block illegal vape sales
thread.title_full: Attorney General Bird leads coalition urging credit card companies to block illegal vape sales

author: Hawkeye Reporter
title: Attorney General Bird leads coalition urging credit card companies to block illegal vape sales
text:
Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird announced on Apr. 15 that she is leading a group of 13 attorneys general in calling on major credit card companies to stop processing transactions for illegal vape products. The coalition sent a letter to Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and Discover, asking them to take action against the sale of unauthorized e-cigarettes and vapes through their payment networks.
The attorneys general say the move is necessary because illegal vapes, mostly made in China, now make up more than 80 percent of all vape sales in the United States and generate over $11 billion annually. They argue that these products are often marketed with candy flavors such as cotton candy and blue raspberry specifically to appeal to children.
“We know that China continues to illegally market candy-flavored vapes, with flavors like cotton candy and blue raspberry, to American kids while they are actually banned in China,” said Attorney General Bird. “These Chinese vapes – and selling them – are illegal. Credit card companies need to work with us to stop the flow of these illegal vapes that are hurting our kids.”
The letter highlights previous cooperation between public agencies and payment processors. In 2005, state attorneys general worked with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives as well as credit card networks to halt internet cigarette sales.
The coalition is urging financial institutions not only to remove merchants selling illicit vapes from their systems but also make public any steps already taken against such transactions. The effort is supported by attorneys general from Alabama, Arkansas, Georgia, Indiana, Kentucky, Montana, Nebraska, North Dakota, South Carolina, South Dakota, Utah and West Virginia.
The group says addressing this issue will help reduce access by minors and curb violations of federal and state laws related to vaping product distribution.
